exposure: changes in maternal dietary intake during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 245 Japanese pregnant women visiting Kyoto Medical Center, with 171 completing nutrition surveys, whose infants were subsequently categorized into small-, appropriate-, or large-for-gestational-age groups.
finding: Higher energy intake throughout pregnancy, and greater consumption of plant oil and sucrose from the first to second trimester, were associated with LGA births.
birth_weight: Babies were categorized as small-for-gestational-age (<10th percentile), appropriate-for-gestational-age (10th-90th percentile), or large-for-gestational-age (>90th percentile) based on birthweight for gestational age.
gest_age: Gestational age was used in conjunction with birthweight to categorize babies into small-, appropriate-, or large-for-gestational-age groups.
